🤥Trump rejects Iran's 7-day peace plan — report
President Trump has rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt regional fighting within seven days, telling aides he expects to resume bombing after November's congressional elections, the Wall Street Journal reports, citing unnamed US officials.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran conveyed its peace plan through Qatari mediators. Under the deal, a seven-day countdown would begin to reopen the Strait and pause regional fighting — including in Lebanon.
💬 "If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araghchi said.
What Iran demands:
🔴 The US lifts its blockade on Iranian ports
🔴 Frozen funds are released
🔴 Oil sanctions are waived
A US official said Washington and Tehran were having "positive and constructive discussions" — but Trump is privately skeptical Iran will meet his demands. He has told staff a renewed bombing campaign is likely.
Meanwhile, the war's regional fallout deepens: Turkey and Pakistan — partners in the Mecca defense pact — met in Riyadh to discuss military coordination, as Yemen's humanitarian crisis worsens and acute malnutrition among children rises.

🚨 Trump rejects Iran’s 7-day plan, eyes renewed bombing — reports
US President Donald Trump has rejected Iran’s proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and told aides he expects US bombing of Iran to resume after the November midterm elections, The Wall Street Journal reported.
Iran’s plan would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and restarted nuclear talks in exchange for the US lifting its naval blockade, unfreezing some Iranian assets and easing restrictions on Iranian oil.
Trump reportedly doubts Iran will accept Washington’s demands and sees renewed strikes as likely.
At the same time, US officials say he is reluctant to launch another major campaign partly because American munitions stocks are dwindling.
